_arc_bridge.from_c3: c3's three-lancets wall is the nave's outer face: three lit windows set in a flat dark wall, the brightest Narthex plate. c4 cornerstone answers by turning the corner — the same ashlar wall, now seen as the nave's side elevation (three dark bays receding) above a lit foundation course. The wall that was the picture in c3 becomes the ground the new picture stands on: the reader has stepped through the lancets' wall and the argument's foundation work begins. Ember→candle handoff: c3's lancet-2 candle is the brightest Narthex light; c4's foundation stone is the first Candle-dominant mass, so the eye reads continuity, not a restart.
_arc_bridge.ladder: IV foundation-band light (stone lit from within at the base) → V full-face light (the whole westwork front kindled, brightest single mass yet) → VI corridor light (light concentrated along the axis, walls fall back — value dips in area but the vanishing bay is the hottest single point yet) → VII split light (two complete lit faces, warmest overall field yet: the whole sky band and both chapels carry value) → VIII sky light (the plate's value moves upward: lit belfry + pale moonlit faces + four town windows; the brightest overall plate, aimed at the crossing lamp above). Area of Candle-bearing pixels and peak value both rise strictly.
_arc_bridge.to_c9: c8's spire is the last exterior plate and the only Nave plate whose light lives in the sky: the lit belfry + moonlit tower faces point the eye upward. c9's crossing lantern answers from directly above — the belfry's four lit lancets rhyme with the lantern ring's four lit lancets (same count, same Candle mass, same stepped crown grammar), so the handoff reads as ascent: town tower below, crossing lantern above, and the hanging lamp is the first light the reader meets INSIDE the room the spire was pointing at.

description: Cohort B covers the Nave arc (Doses IV–VIII): the reader is inside the building now, walking the nave bay by bay while the candlelight spreads. Foundation (p1c4) → the Cathedral's portrait (p1c5 flagship) → receding arcade (p1c6) → parting side-chapels (p1c7) → the tower above the town (p1c8). Nave grammar per ART-DIRECTION.md §6: light value + depth grow strictly IV→VIII; one flame grammar copied from art/cover.svg throughout (wax #E8DCC2 + ember→gold flame + stepped flat spill wedges, never blur). Supervisor merges sequentially into design/chapters.json per READER-CONTRACT §4.

p1c4.caption: Dose IV · The cornerstone
p1c4.content_rationale: Ch.4 lays the joint-stock foundation and the unity-of-command apex-stone: Plan Moldbug (para 16), the capital-as-real-estate (para 97), a single load-bearing authority (para 100) — replacement, never repair (para 123). The plate stages that argumentative act: c3's lit lancet wall turned the corner into the nave's dark side-elevation, its three bays receding above a full-width foundation course; ONE proud drafted stone stands centered in the course, washed in the chapter's first orange, carrying a single candle. One stone carries one flame: unity of command, drawn.
p1c4.end_seal: Drafted cornerstone block: Candle-outline square with tooled inner margin + centered gold flame pip, in Dose IV tint #B65729 (url() ≤32px, contract A.0).

grounds.quote: we have four little paint chips from the real picture. We know something is weird, because each of the chips is orange—and there is no orange on the official picture.
grounds.why: The cornerstone's Candle wash is the chapter's first orange on the official picture: the new color entering the dark wall, exactly as the chips entered the argument.

grounds.quote: UR’s cure for the monetary blues, hereafter to be known as Plan Moldbug, is (a) instantaneously effective, (b) thoroughly fair, (c) certain to be wildly popular, and (d) results in a stable, free-market monetary system.
grounds.why: The plate's single proud lit stone is the Plan itself: one precisely specified foundation-stone, drawn whole and complete, worthy of the candle it carries.

grounds.quote: The capital is the country, i.e., its real estate. The value of real estate is its price.
grounds.why: The foundation course is the country's capital drawn as real estate: the band of great blocks whose value the candlelight reveals is literally land-value made visible.

grounds.quote: the formula for authority is clear: unity of command. A single extremely capable individual can manage an organization of any size
grounds.why: One stone, not many, carries the candle: the cornerstone is the unity-of-command apex drawn as a single load-bearing block.

grounds.quote: it’s fatally broken, and needs to be replaced by something completely different. Even in Carlyle’s day, repair did not seem like an option.
grounds.why: Nothing is repaired in the plate — the dark old wall stands untouched while the NEW lit course is laid beneath it: replacement, not renovation, with zero GI1 breakage.

p1c4.palette_role: Nave floor: first Candle-dominant mass in the book (the cornerstone wash + spill wedges); Sanctuary Red confined to the flame base. Wall and sky stay Narthex-dark so the foundation light reads as an arrival, not a gradient.

p1c4.title: Plan Moldbug

p1c5.caption: Dose V · The westwork
p1c5.content_rationale: Ch.5 is the commissioned portrait of USG in the large (para 0): the small-c constitution as actual structure of power (para 15), restored in attention and never ruined (para 10). The plate faces the reader frontally at the cohort's largest scale: twin towers, a gallery of ten identical evenly-lit openings (press rank above, university rank below — homogeneity as architecture, paras 135/137), a blind oculus with a gold heart set above every door (sovereignty above all other powers, para 125), three portals ajar, one great candle before the center. The whole face glows though no lamp hangs in any opening: self-coordination without central administration (para 143) — a lit building with no one in it.
p1c5.end_seal: Westwork seal: twin-tower outline with a centered gold oculus between the towers, in Dose V tint #BB622A (url() ≤32px, contract A.0).

grounds.quote: I feel we are ready for our portrait of USG in the large—what she is, and how she came to be.
grounds.why: The plate IS the commissioned portrait: USG in the large, faced frontally like a sitter, at the largest scale the cohort allows.

grounds.quote: No—the program of the archist is not destruction, but restoration.
grounds.why: The westwork stands whole and lit — every tower, arch, and opening intact: the portrait honors the archist program by showing the building restored in attention, never ruined (GI1 as content).

grounds.quote: a government’s constitution (small c) is its actual structure of power.
grounds.why: The plate draws the small-c constitution: not a document but the actual structure — walls, galleries, portals — the process by which the building formulates its decisions.

grounds.quote: The sovereign power is the power that is above all other powers.
grounds.why: The blind oculus centered above the three portals: sovereignty located as a single gold-hearted eye set higher than every door — above all other powers, drawn.

grounds.quote: all are the same. And the same is true of news desks at the major centers of journalism.
grounds.why: The gallery's two identical ranks are the Ivy League row and the news desks: same size, same light, interchangeable — homogeneity as architecture.

grounds.quote: what we don’t see is any hierarchical coordinating authority. But what we do see is actual coordination.
grounds.why: Ten identical evenly-lit gallery openings with no larger central window and no crown: coordination (uniform light) without a coordinator (no head) — the chapter's central paradox, drawn.

grounds.quote: And thus, an information machine without any central administration self-coordinates and achieves effective censorship.
grounds.why: The whole face glows though no lamp hangs in any opening: the light has no visible source but the one candle before the building — self-coordination without central administration.

The opener feels like entering the portrait gallery: plate given air, meta block centered.

End seal ≤32px westwork in Dose V tint (#BB622A).
p1c5.title: The Modern Structure

p1c6.caption: Dose VI · The arcade
p1c6.content_rationale: Ch.6 strings history's beads on theory's string (para 0): the Mugwump→Progressive winners remembered, Brother Jonathan disappeared like the dog that did not bark (para 27). The plate draws that double motion in one figure: four nested arch orders (Mackay, Adams, the Mugwumps — beads on the perspective axis) recede to a gold vanishing bay, the lofty rostrum above democracy (para 63); the left piers catch candlelight bound order-to-order like progressive mortar (para 76) while the right piers fall dark — whole but hollow husks (para 89), unlit stone, never erasure. The near orders crouch low beside the soaring bay: miniscule stultified Washington dwarfed by the Structure it becomes (para 54).
p1c6.end_seal: Arcade seal: three nested arch outlines, left half gold / right half dark, in Dose VI tint #C06D2C (url() ≤32px, contract A.0).

grounds.quote: If history is a necklace, theory is the string. Now, some beads.
grounds.why: The receding orders are the string drawn in stone: each arch-ring a bead (Mackay, Adams, the Mugwumps) threaded on the single perspective axis toward the vanishing bay.

grounds.quote: What is strange is that the dog would not bark in the night—that a national metonym could just disappear.
grounds.why: The dark right-hand piers are the dog that did not bark: the arcade's shadowed half where Brother Jonathan stood and no longer stands — disappearance drawn as unlit stone, not erasure.

grounds.quote: Washington, paralyzed by the struggle between North and South, was by postwar standards miniscule and stultified.
grounds.why: The near orders are low and cramped beside the soaring lit vanishing bay: the miniscule stultified Washington dwarfed by the Structure it becomes.

grounds.quote: What Adams and the Mugwumps are asking for is no less than the creation of a new power structure, a 'lofty rostrum,' which is above democracy—
grounds.why: The vanishing bay glows ABOVE the arcade floor line, elevated and apart: the lofty rostrum above democracy, the corridor's bright end.

grounds.quote: Progressivism, big or small P, being the religion of government in our time, the distributed delusion of our atheistic theocracy. The mortar, as it were, in the Modern Structure.
grounds.why: The Candle wash binding the left piers order-to-order is the mortar: the progressive religion holding the winners' arcade together, course by course.

grounds.quote: leaving the empty, powerless husk of formerly private religious organizations such as the YMCA—once, believe it or not, a force in the land.
grounds.why: The dark right-hand arches are drawn whole but hollow — intact outlines with nothing inside: husks, emptied but unbroken (GI1).

p1c6.opener_composition: #chapter-art.arch plate → 'DOSE VI · PART I' → Marcellus title 'Brother Jonathan' → candle rule → calm body. The plate's strong center axis suits a centered meta block; the corridor aims the eye down into the title.
p1c6.palette_role: Mid-nave concentration: total Candle area narrows (corridor, not facade) but peak value rises — the vanishing bay (.5 flat gold) is the hottest single mass yet. The lit-left/dark-right split is the cohort's first composed shadow-mass, previewing c7's two-chapel split.
p1c6.reading_treatment: Quiet body ≤68ch; 92 paras, the cohort's shortest — the plate carries the chapter's visual weight. Marcellus Candle drop cap 'S' on 'So at least we have a theory of the Modern Structure…' (190 chars, theory-then-beads hinge — warranted). End seal ≤32px split arcade in Dose VI tint (#C06D2C).
p1c6.title: Brother Jonathan

p1c7.caption: Dose VII · Two chapels
p1c7.content_rationale: Ch.7 tries the Modern Wars under the UPP settlement: two governments divided by the present line of military control, each recognizing the other as a sovereign peer (para 24) — two conflicting perspectives given equal weight (para 32), a marriage over with each party under its own roof (para 99). The plate draws separation as the chapter defines it: two COMPLETE gabled chapels of identical massing (shared ridge height, eaves line, quoins) on one continuous ground, split by empty night air with a surveyor's boundary stone at the gap's foot. The warm right chapel burns on (the plaintiff, continuing); the moonlit left chapel rests stopped where it is (the defendant, content, para 27) — asymmetry of will, never of wholeness. The right chapel's warm wash is the glass-and-concrete castle's ancestor (para 3). GI1 absolute: two wholes, never one wounded whole.
p1c7.end_seal: Twin-chapel seal: two tiny gabled outlines with a gap between, right one gold-filled, in Dose VII tint #C6782F (url() ≤32px, contract A.0).

grounds.quote: how we got from a few well-meaning Mugwumps to Kafka’s castle in glass and concrete—the vast, sclerotic and depressing Modern Structure.
grounds.why: The right chapel's warm wash against the night is the castle's ancestor: the modern side already glowing with the institutional life that becomes the glass-and-concrete castle.

grounds.quote: The new boundary between the governments is the present line of military control. Each recognizes the other as a sovereign peer under classical international law.
grounds.why: The empty night band + boundary stone IS the UPP settlement drawn: a surveyed line between two governments, each whole, each recognized — the plate's entire composition.

grounds.quote: the plaintiff is the party that wants to continue the war. The defendant is the party that would be happy to let it stop where it is.
grounds.why: The lit right chapel burns on (the plaintiff, continuing); the moonlit left chapel rests stopped where it is (the defendant, content) — asymmetry of will, not of wholeness.

grounds.quote: we have two conflicting perspectives with which to examine the Modern Wars.
grounds.why: Two chapels, two lightings, one ground: the two perspectives (modern verdict / synthetic hypothesis) given equal architectural weight, neither demolished.

grounds.quote: It should have been clear by the 1830s that the marriage with Puritan revolutionary democracy was not a winner.
grounds.why: Two separate houses, not one divided house: the marriage is over and each party has its own roof — secession as departure, both dwellings intact.

p1c7.opener_composition: #chapter-art.arch plate centered full-slot-width so the bilateral separation reads instantly → 'DOSE VII · PART I' → Marcellus title 'The War of Secession' → candle rule → calm body. Symmetric verdict composition (sibling to c2's twin-arch logic), not a journey.
p1c7.palette_role: Warmest field yet: the right chapel's Candle wash + the sky band lift the plate's total value past c6 while the gap stays Narthex-dark — the arc's first plate whose brightest region is OFF-center. Sanctuary Red only in the flame base. Vellum appears as moonlight (tympanum + wash), previewing c8's moonlit tower.
p1c7.reading_treatment: Quiet body ≤68ch; 158 paras of trial-before-verdict need zero opener interference. Marcellus Candle drop cap 'I' on 'It occurs to me that the previous chapter may have fallen a bit short of its surgical purpose.' (94 chars, the surgical-purpose line re-opening the operation the plate stages — warranted). End seal ≤32px twin chapels in Dose VII tint (#C6782F).
p1c7.title: The War of Secession

p1c8.caption: Dose VIII · The spire
p1c8.content_rationale: Ch.8 compresses the 20th century to narrative coherence (para 16): Olde Towne Easte and the crumbled mansions of the town pillars (para 10) — yet 'its dwellings remain, mostly' (para 9), and what killed the builders was USG, the ghost haunting the town (para 155). The plate draws one tower, four houses, one sky: a tall parish tower with a moonlit spire and four glowing belfry lancets (the rhyme c9's lantern answers), an ajar portal with one candle, and four whole lit merchants' houses — the answer to Piranesi's Rome-with-cows (para 169) drawn in Piranesi's own medium, but with the Forum's roof still on. Brightest overall Nave plate; the value moves into the sky half, aimed upward at the crossing to come.
p1c8.end_seal: Spire seal: tower-and-spire outline with four gold belfry ticks, in Dose VIII tint #CC8333 (url() ≤32px, contract A.0).

grounds.quote: The world that built these mansions—the Midwest of Booth Tarkington (have a look at Penrod if you want to see Middle America before progressivism)—is no less dust than the Caesars. Yet its dwellings remain, mostly.
grounds.why: 'Yet its dwellings remain': the town stands intact around the tower — dust for the builders, endurance for the buildings; the plate draws the remains, not the dust.

grounds.quote: what happened to Olde Towne Easte? Why did it decline? Why did the mansions of the town pillars of Columbus crumble?
grounds.why: The flanking town houses ARE Olde Towne Easte: the dwellings of the town pillars, drawn whole and lit — the question hangs over them, and the plate refuses the ruin-answer (GI1).

grounds.quote: Our aim in this chapter is to restore narrative coherence to the 20th century, ridding it of mystical obfuscations, poltergeists, and winds of change.
grounds.why: One tower, four houses, one sky: the century compressed to a single legible veduta — narrative coherence drawn as architectural clarity, no poltergeists.

grounds.quote: It is as gone as Caesar’s ghost. What killed it? The same thing that killed everything else. USG.
grounds.why: The moonlit (dead, cold) spire faces against the warm living town windows: the ghost of the old order haunting — but intact above — the town USG killed.

grounds.quote: Piranesi’s Rome, cows in the Forum and all. Though I’m not sure Cleveland is safe for cows.
grounds.why: The plate answers Piranesi with Piranesi: a veduta of tower-and-town in the Carceri medium (bitten line + tonal mass) — but where Piranesi drew ruins, GI1 draws the Forum with its roof still on.

p1c8.opener_composition: #chapter-art.arch plate → 'DOSE VIII · PART I' → Marcellus title 'Olde Towne Easte' → candle rule → calm body. The plate's vertical thrust suits a centered meta block beneath; the spire aims past the title toward the crossing to come.
p1c8.palette_role: Nave crown and brightest overall: first plate with value in the sky half (belfry gold + moonlit spire + Vellum town windows). Candle owns belfry + portal + wedges; Vellum carries domestic window-light (its first architectural use since the stars). Hands the arc upward to c9's lantern: belfry four ≈ lantern four.

p1c8.title: Olde Towne Easte
